nodes.name: Copper substrate preparation
nodes.procedure: Electrolytic copper disks (14 mm diameter, 2 mm thickness) were mechanically polished up to 2400 grit size by emery papers. Final polishing using 0.05 μm alumina powder, then cleaned ultrasonically in ethanol for 30 min. Electropolishing at 20 mA cm⁻² for 1 min in solution containing 70 g L⁻¹ Na₂CO₃, 10 g L⁻¹ KOH, 10 g L⁻¹ sodium dodecyl sulfate (C₁₂H₂₅NaO₄S). Washed, activated in 10 wt% HCl for 20 s at room temperature, washed in distilled water, immediately placed in electrodeposition bath.

nodes.name: Primary Ni layer electrodeposition (first step)
nodes.procedure: All electrodepositions performed in 500 mL beaker. Copper substrate (working electrode) and platinum plate (counter electrode) placed vertically, parallel, 1 cm apart, 1 cm from beaker bottom. Magnetic stirrer at 300 rpm between electrodes. Primary Ni deposit applied using Ni bath (NiCl₂·6H₂O 238 g L⁻¹ as metal source, H₃BO₃ 40 g L⁻¹ as pH buffer, NH₄Cl 200 g L⁻¹ as crystal modifier) at constant current density 20 mA cm⁻² for 10 min.
nodes.source_text: 2.2. Electrodeposition procedure... first step... 20 mA cm⁻² for 10 min.

nodes.name: Ni-Co second layer electrodeposition
nodes.procedure: Second Ni-Co layer deposited on primary Ni layer using Ni-Co plating bath (same as Ni bath + CoCl₂·6H₂O 40 g L⁻¹) at constant current density of 50 mA cm⁻² for 1-3 min. Bath at pH 4, temperature 60±0.1°C, magnetic stirring 300 rpm. Samples quickly transferred between baths for dual coatings.
nodes.source_text: 2.2. Electrodeposition procedure... second-step layer... 50 mA cm⁻² at different deposition times (1, 2 and 3 min).

nodes.name: Ni-Co first layer electrodeposition
nodes.procedure: Primary Ni-Co deposit applied on Cu substrate using Ni-Co plating bath at constant current density of 20 mA cm⁻² for 10 min. Bath at pH 4, temperature 60±0.1°C, magnetic stirring 300 rpm.

nodes.name: Ni second layer electrodeposition
nodes.procedure: Second Ni layer deposited on primary Ni-Co layer using Ni plating bath at constant current density of 50 mA cm⁻² for 1-3 min. Bath at pH 4, temperature 60±0.1°C, magnetic stirring 300 rpm.

nodes.source_text: Erosion-corrosion behaviour of the coatings was evaluated in 1 L of a slurry solution at pH 7, containing 40 wt%/o SiO2 + 3.5 wt%/o NaCl. The size of the SiO2 particles was in the range of 200-300 μm and the rotational speed was 500 rpm... The decrease of water contact angles raised by erosion-corrosion are 8.3, for NC3 coatings
The Ni-Co/Ni experienced the lowest degradation during erosion-corrosion test... The decrease of water contact angles raised by erosion-corrosion are 10.5, for CN1
The Ni/Ni coating showed the highest increase of polarization resistance after erosion-corrosion test... The decrease of water contact angles raised by erosion-corrosion are 14.2, for NN3
The decrease of water contact angles raised by erosion-corrosion are 7.6, for CC1

nodes.characterization_summary: NC3 coating shows Ni cones fully covered by flower-like Ni-Co deposits (<100 nm height for NC1, 200 nm height/140 nm width for NC2, 300 nm height/190 nm width for NC3).
nodes.evidence_snippet: Fig. 2 represents surface morphologies of the dual Ni/Ni-Co coatings produced after second deposition steps of 1, 2 and 3 min (i.e. NC1, NC2 & NC3 samples, respectively).

nodes.characterization_summary: CN1 coating shows Ni-Co flower-like morphology unaffected by 1 min Ni deposition; CN2 shows cones 300 nm height/190 nm width; CN3 shows cones 330 nm height/220 nm width.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Fig. 3 represents the surface morphology of the dual Ni-Co/Ni coatings soon after second deposition steps of 1, 2 and 3 min (i.e. CN1, CN2 & CN3, respectively).

nodes.characterization_summary: NN3 shows conical array morphology explained by BCF theory; CC1 shows flower-like deposits explained by MIDL theory.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The conical array of Ni coatings can be explained according to the Burton-Cabrera-Frank (BCF) theory.
Results of the Dual and pure Ni-Co coatings composition evaluated by on top surface EDS maps are presented in Table 2.

nodes.characterization_summary: All coatings show average thickness of 5.6 ± 0.3 μm; NC3 second layer thickness 2.3 μm; CN1 second layer thickness <1 μm.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The average thickness of the obtained coatings is 5 . 6 ~ \pm ~ 0 . 3 \mu \mathrm { m } and the calculated value for each coating is reported in the right side of SEM images in Fig. 10.

nodes.characterization_summary: All coatings show FCC Ni reflections at (111), (200), (220), (311) planes; no cobalt containing phase observed; Ni peaks shift to lower angles with increasing Co content.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Typical reflections of FCC Ni crystal, compatible with JCPDS file card #04-0850, can be observed and related to (111), (200), (220), (311) planes.

nodes.characterization_summary: NC3: Ra=0.46 μm, RRMS=0.62 μm, RSk=0.24, Rku=4.26; CN1: Ra=0.34 μm, RRMS=0.49 μm, RSk=-2.41, Rku=10.03; NN3: Ra=0.56 μm, RRMS=0.74 μm, RSk=0.54, Rku=4.07; CC1: Ra=0.40 μm, RRMS=0.51 μm, RSk=0.58, Rku=3.43.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Roughness parameters of the coatings are reported in Table 5. The average roughness ( R _ { a } ) of the as polished Cu substrate is around 0 . 0 3 \mu \mathrm { m }.

nodes.characterization_summary: Thick Ni coating (NN3): 583 ± 38 Hv; thick Ni-Co coating (CC1): 671 ± 60 Hv (10 N load, ASTM E 384-05A).
nodes.evidence_snippet: Micro-hardness values for Ni and Ni-Co coatings under an applied load of 1 0 \mathrm { N } were obtained to be 5 8 3 ~ \pm ~ 3 8 ~ and 6 7 1 ~ \pm ~ 6 0 \mathrm { H v } , respectively.

nodes.characterization_summary: After erosion-corrosion, NiO vibrational modes detected: 1TO at ~370 cm⁻¹, 1LO at ~509 cm⁻¹, TO+LO at ~863 cm⁻¹, 2LO at ~1070 cm⁻¹; lowest 1LO peak intensity for CN1.
nodes.evidence_snippet: In the Raman spectra, the vibrational modes of NiO are revealed by the one-phonon 1TO (at ~ 3 7 0 \mathrm { c m } ^ { - 1 } ) and 1LO (at ~ 5 0 9 \mathrm { c m } ^ { - 1 } ) peaks.

nodes.characterization_summary: All coatings show (111) preferred orientation: NC3 (111) TC=1.5; CN1 (111) TC=1.5; NN3 (111) TC=1.9; CC1 (111) TC=1.5. RTC shows >35% (111) planes.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The results of TC measurement are reported in Table 3. It can be seen that all the coatings have (111) plane as their preferred crystalline orientation.
